commits.message:
Automate badge updates with PR creation

Add permission for pull-requests and switch badge regeneration to dry-run. The workflow now runs `update-my-badges` with `--dryrun` and then uses peter-evans/create-pull-request to open a branch (`chore/update-achievement-badges`) with a commit and PR titled "chore: update dynamic achievement badges`. The PR is configured to include an explanatory body and to delete the branch after merging. This prevents direct pushes and makes badge updates reviewable.
commits.messageBody: Add permission for pull-requests and switch badge regeneration to dry-run. The workflow now runs `update-my-badges` with `--dryrun` and then uses peter-evans/create-pull-request to open a branch (`chore/update-achievement-badges`) with a commit and PR titled "chore: update dynamic achievement badges`. The PR is configured to include an explanatory body and to delete the branch after merging. This prevents direct pushes and makes badge updates reviewable.

commits.message:
Add Node.js 22 setup to badges workflow

Insert a setup-node step into .github/workflows/my-badges.yml to install Node.js 22 LTS using actions/setup-node@v4. This ensures the workflow has Node 22 available before running the dynamic achievement badge generation step, which is likely required by the badge generation tooling.
commits.messageBody: Insert a setup-node step into .github/workflows/my-badges.yml to install Node.js 22 LTS using actions/setup-node@v4. This ensures the workflow has Node 22 available before running the dynamic achievement badge generation step, which is likely required by the badge generation tooling.

commits.message:
Add debug env and simplify badge command

Expose GITHUB_USER and GITHUB_REPO as env vars and print token length, user and repo for debugging Actions permissions. Keep the existing empty-token check, and simplify the npx update-my-badges invocation to pass only the repository owner and remove explicit --repo/--token flags (retain --compact and --size=56). This helps troubleshoot badge generation and reduces command arguments.
commits.messageBody: Expose GITHUB_USER and GITHUB_REPO as env vars and print token length, user and repo for debugging Actions permissions. Keep the existing empty-token check, and simplify the npx update-my-badges invocation to pass only the repository owner and remove explicit --repo/--token flags (retain --compact and --size=56). This helps troubleshoot badge generation and reduces command arguments.

commits.message:
Check GITHUB_TOKEN and pass it to update-my-badges

Add a guard that fails the job with a clear message when GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, and update the npx update-my-badges invocation to pass --repo and --token so the action runs with explicit repository and token parameters.
commits.messageBody: Add a guard that fails the job with a clear message when GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, and update the npx update-my-badges invocation to pass --repo and --token so the action runs with explicit repository and token parameters.

commits.message:
Use npx --yes and remove README badge wrapper

Add --yes to the update-my-badges invocation in the GitHub Actions workflow to avoid interactive prompts during CI. Also remove the surrounding <div> wrapper in README around the my-badges markers to simplify markup and prevent layout issues.
commits.messageBody: Add --yes to the update-my-badges invocation in the GitHub Actions workflow to avoid interactive prompts during CI. Also remove the surrounding <div> wrapper in README around the my-badges markers to simplify markup and prevent layout issues.

commits.message:
Switch my-badges action to npx update-my-badges

Replace the my-badges/my-badges@master action step with a direct npx invocation of update-my-badges. The workflow now exports GITHUB_TOKEN via env and runs `npx update-my-badges "${{ github.repository_owner }}" --compact --size=56`, preserving the previous compact and size options while using the CLI instead of the action.
commits.messageBody: Replace the my-badges/my-badges@master action step with a direct npx invocation of update-my-badges. The workflow now exports GITHUB_TOKEN via env and runs `npx update-my-badges "${{ github.repository_owner }}" --compact --size=56`, preserving the previous compact and size options while using the CLI instead of the action.

commits.message:
Force Node24 for JS actions and bump checkout

Add env FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true to ensure JavaScript actions run on Node 24, and upgrade actions/checkout from v4 to v5. This updates the workflow to target the newer Node runtime for JS actions and pull in fixes/features from the latest checkout action.

commits.message:
Use my-badges action from master

Update workflow to use my-badges/my-badges@master instead of the v0.4.0 tag so the job pulls the latest action from the default branch. This changes the reference from a fixed tag to a branch ref, which may affect reproducibility — consider pinning to a tag if deterministic behavior is required.

This changes the reference from a fixed tag to a branch ref, which may affect reproducibility — consider pinning to a tag if deterministic behavior is required.

commits.message:
Run badges workflow on push to main

Add a push trigger for the main branch to .github/workflows/my-badges.yml so the 'Update achievements badges' workflow runs on pushes to main in addition to manual dispatch and the existing cron schedule. Ensures badge updates occur immediately after changes are merged to main.
commits.messageBody: Add a push trigger for the main branch to .github/workflows/my-badges.yml so the 'Update achievements badges' workflow runs on pushes to main in addition to manual dispatch and the existing cron schedule. Ensures badge updates occur immediately after changes are merged to main.

commits.message:
Add my-badges workflow, update README badges

Add a new GitHub Actions workflow (my-badges.yml) to generate dynamic achievement badges (scheduled daily and workflow_dispatch) using my-badges/my-badges@v0.4.0. Update README.md: include iOS/Swift and C++ in skill lists and badges, adjust table/layout widths, replace legacy GitHub stats/graphs with profile-summary cards and revamped activity/trophy sections, and add an Achievements placeholder to be populated by the new workflow. These changes improve README visuals and enable automated achievement badges.
